title: Halting of the matrix computation
statement: Let $a,b,f,B$ be natural numbers, let $m$ be a Boolean mode, let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, and let $x$ and $\beta$ be finite Boolean strings. Suppose a fifteen-register state $st$ has every register at most $B$, and its registers $u,t,c,z$ are zero. On input the pairing of $x$ and $\beta$, the register program starting in its matrix-computation instruction with register values $st$ halts while satisfying the program guard at every time before halting. Its answer is true when $m$ is true; otherwise it is true exactly when there is an edge for input $x$ and radius $s$ from vertex $\lfloor i/(2\cdot 2^e)\rfloor$ to vertex $\lfloor (i/2)\bmod 2^e\rfloor$, where $s,i,e$ are the corresponding registers of $st$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols
all fifteen registers of $st$ are at most $B$
replaced:
Let $a,b,f,B$ be nonnegative integers, let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing
machine with Boolean tape symbols, and let $x,\beta$ be finite bit strings. Consider the
program $A$ with parameters $a,b,f$ and mode
$\mathrm{mode}\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, supplied with the five-language
oracle associated to $N$. For a register state $\mathrm{st}$, suppose each of its
fifteen registers is at most $B$, and its registers $u,t,c,z$ are all zero. Starting the
program in its matrix-computation state with register values given by $\mathrm{st}$, on
input encoding the pair $(x,\beta)$, it halts with its registers bounded by $B$ at every
earlier step; its answer is true if the mode is true, and otherwise is the truth value
of whether there is an edge, for input $x$ and radius $s$, from vertex $\left\lfloor
i/(4\cdot 2^e)\right\rfloor$ to vertex $\left\lfloor (i/2)\bmod 2^e\right\rfloor$, where
$s,i,e$ are the corresponding registers of $\mathrm{st}$.
